support.name: Support agent
support.desc: Answers from your docs and saved pages, files bug reports in Track and hands off to a human when unsure.
support.welcome: Hi! I'm the support assistant. How can I help?
support.instructions:
You are the support assistant for our company. Your goal is to resolve customer questions quickly and accurately.

How to work:
- Always search the knowledge base before answering a question about the product, pricing, policies or how-tos.
- Answer in 1–4 short sentences. Use simple steps when explaining how to do something.
- If the customer reports a bug or something broken, ask for the minimum details (what they did, what happened, their email) and create an issue in Track with a clear title and those details. Tell them the team will follow up.
- If the answer is not in the knowledge base, do not guess: say so and hand off to a human.
- If the customer is upset, asks for a refund, a cancellation or a person, hand off to a human.

Tone: friendly, calm and direct. No marketing language.

sdr.name: Sales SDR that books meetings
sdr.desc: Answers product questions, captures the lead in the CRM and books a demo in your Cal event type.
sdr.welcome: Hi! Want to see how we can help your team? I can answer questions or book a quick demo.
sdr.instructions:
You are a friendly sales development rep. Your goal is to understand what the visitor needs, answer their questions and, when there is interest, book a demo.

How to work:
- Answer product and pricing questions only from the knowledge base.
- Ask at most one question at a time: their company, team size and what they want to solve.
- When they show interest, offer a demo. Check availability and offer 3 concrete times in their timezone (ask for it if unknown).
- Before booking, confirm the exact time and ask for their full name and work email. Book only after they confirm.
- Save the lead in the CRM with their email, name and a short note of what they need.
- If they ask about custom contracts, security reviews or anything you can't answer, hand off to a human.

Tone: warm, concise and never pushy.

qualifier.name: Lead qualifier
qualifier.desc: Asks your qualification questions, saves the answers as a CRM note and routes hot leads to your team.
qualifier.welcome: Hi! A few quick questions so we can point you to the right person.
qualifier.instructions:
You qualify inbound leads for our sales team.

Ask these questions, one at a time, in a natural way:
1. What is your name and work email?
2. What company do you work for and how many people are on your team?
3. What problem are you trying to solve?
4. When do you need a solution (this month, this quarter, later)?
5. Do you have a budget assigned?

When you have the email, create or update the contact in the CRM. When you have all the answers, add a note with a short summary and a score: HOT (needs it this quarter and has budget), WARM or COLD.
For HOT leads, hand off to a human so sales follows up right away. For the rest, thank them and say the team will be in touch.

Never make up answers the visitor did not give. Keep messages short.

reasonEmpty.model_failure: The AI model did not answer

replay.title: Replay real conversations
replay.hint: Sends the first messages of the last 10 real conversations to the saved draft (simulated, nothing runs) and compares what it answered then with what it answers now.
replay.empty: No real conversations to replay yet.

procedures.title: Procedures
procedures.hint: Step-by-step flows the agent follows in order, with questions, branches and actions. It starts with a keyword or when the agent recognizes the case. The visitor can write “cancel” to leave it.
procedures.lastMessage: Thanks, we have everything we need.
procedures.name: Name
procedures.triggerPlaceholder: The visitor wants a refund for an order
procedures.triggerHint: The agent reads this to decide when to start. Keywords start it right away.
procedures.question: Question
procedures.argsHint: One per line: name = value. Use '{{variable}}' for saved answers and '{{result.field}}' for tool results.

issues.bad_goto: This step jumps to a step that no longer exists.
issues.ask_needs_field: Name the variable where the answer is saved.
issues.tool_off: Pick a tool and turn it on in the Tools tab.
issues.form_missing: Pick a form (create it under Forms).
issues.branch_needs_condition: Complete the condition and the step to go to.
issues.duplicate_id: Two steps share the same id.
issues.loop: This step jumps back without a question in between: it would repeat forever.

forms.title: Forms
forms.hint: Forms the agent can show inside the chat, or as a procedure step. With “Save in the CRM”, each submission creates or updates the contact with a note.
forms.name: Name
forms.needsEmail: Add an email field to save the contact.
forms.label: Label

code.unavailable: Code runs in Vercel Sandbox. On this server it is not set up, so calls return code_unavailable.
code.name: Function name
code.description: What it does (the agent reads this)
code.codeHint: The body of an async function that receives input with the parameters and returns JSON. No network access.

integrations.adminsOnly: Only admins and owners can connect services.
integrations.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect {name}? The agent stops using it right away.

hints.stripe: Use a restricted key with read access to customers, subscriptions and invoices.
hints.shopify: Create a custom app in your Shopify admin with read access to orders and products, and paste its Admin API token.
hints.slack: Create a Slack app with a bot (app_mentions:read, im:history, chat:write), install it and paste the bot token and the signing secret.
hints.meta: In your Meta app, generate a Page access token (pages_messaging, and instagram_manage_messages for Instagram) and paste it with the app secret.

sources.title: Zendesk help center
sources.hint: Articles of a public Zendesk help center, read in the background and refreshed every day. Up to 3 help centers.
sources.docsImport: Notion and Confluence come in through Docs: import them and their pages work as knowledge.

semantic.title: Semantic search
semantic.hint: Finds the right passage even when the question uses other words. Indexing uses AI tokens; search keeps working by keywords while it indexes.

ab.title: A/B test
ab.hint: A saved version answers part of the new conversations and the rest keep the live one. Compare them and keep the better one.
ab.needsVersions: Publish at least two versions to run a test.
ab.running: Version {number} answers {percent}% of new conversations since {since}.
ab.promoteConfirm: Put version {number} live for everyone and end the test?
ab.stopConfirm: End the test? All new conversations go back to the live version.
ab.noVersions: There is no other saved version to test yet.

access.title: Who can see and edit
access.hint: Admins and owners edit every agent. Members see agents read only unless you change it here. Secrets, MCP servers and connections stay with admins.
